name: Oxalis

project_scope.target_zone_status: County nativity UNRESOLVED for all four canonical members; O. stricta additionally has an explicit Texas-native distribution CONFLICT. Never promote either status by implication.
project_scope.source_pool_note: Oxalis albicans is included in the five-taxon approved family teaching scope but has no canonical species page at this check; show as pending, not an installed fifth species.

look_here_first: FIRST find where the leaves attach. Leaves all at the ground with separate LEAFLESS flower stalks? Compare the two purple bulbous woodsorrels. Leaves carried up branching green stems? Compare yellow woodsorrels under magnification. NEXT compare matching leaflets or stem hairs, not just the flower color.

study_strategy.teaching_sequence: SEE the whole plant → SPOT basal leaves vs leafy stems → NAME bulb/scape/notch/hairs → COMPARE same-scale diagnostic parts → REMEMBER the caution
shared_traits: Three leaflets on a common leaf stalk (TRIFOLIOLATE). Each leaflet is often heart-shaped or notched at the tip.
Flowers typically have five petals; the family has ten stamens in two length groups and a five-celled ovary.
Fruits are capsules; mature capsule and seed close-ups help when leaves and flowers overlap.
Some species grow from bulbs with leaves clustered at the base; others have leaves on visible branching stems.
priority: 1. WHOLE PLANT: trace leaves to basal bulb or above-ground stem; a close-up of only one leaf misses the first split.
2. BULBOUS PAIR: match leaflet notch depth and width in millimeters; investigate pale oxalate lines along notch margins.
3. YELLOW STEMMED PAIR: inspect stem and node hairs in macro/microscope photos—straight pressed-forward vs spreading hairs, including septate hairs.
4. FRUIT: use ripe capsule length and seeds only as secondary supporting clues.
5. LOCAL LOOK-ALIKE: creeping O. corniculata may root at stem nodes and show conspicuous broad stipule wings at petiole bases.
study_strategy.warning: Purple petals do NOT prove O. violacea, and yellow petals do NOT identify O. dillenii versus O. stricta. Leaflet width and flower counts overlap; hairs may need 10–20× magnification. Retain unidentified Oxalis sp. when key structures are absent.

quick_key.if: Basal leaves emerge from a bulb; flower stalks are separate and leafless
quick_key.then: Bulbous Oxalis: compare O. drummondii and O. violacea

quick_key.if: Bulbous, broadly notched leaflets often 14–34 mm long, often deeply lobed; oxalate lines near notch absent
quick_key.then: Oxalis drummondii — two exact-species reference photos now installed; still needs measured notch and orange sepal-tip tubercle macros

quick_key.if: Bulbous, leaflets often 8–15 mm long, shallower notch; oxalate lines along notch margins
quick_key.then: Oxalis violacea — verify matched leaf macros, not violet flower color

quick_key.if: Leafy aerial stems, yellow flowers, straight forward-appressed NONSEPTATE hairs
quick_key.then: Oxalis dillenii — verify multiple nodes and mature capsules

quick_key.if: Leafy aerial stems, yellow flowers, spreading hairs including SEPTATE hairs at nodes
quick_key.then: Oxalis stricta — concept/range CONFLICT; do not claim local nativity

quick_key.if: Short curved/crisped nonseptate stem hairs on a yellow woodsorrel
quick_key.then: Oxalis albicans — approved comparison target, NOT YET a canonical learner page

quick_key.if: Creeping stems root at nodes with broad stipule flanges
quick_key.then: Check Oxalis corniculata, a look-alike outside this four-species canonical set

visual_comparison.title: Four installed woodsorrels — learn the real plant before the tiny anatomy
visual_comparison.subtitle: Eight actual physically installed exact-species views across four canonical woodsorrels. Whole-plant and flower/fruit reference roles are confirmed, but matched-mm notch and microscopic stem-hair differences still await verified photos.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: GROUND + separate stalks = purple bulbous pair. LEAFY STEM + yellow flower = hairs and nodes. Notch depth and stem hairs win over petal color.
